extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing biomedical research manuscripts for submission to Cell or similar high-profile journals; researchers seeking professional English editing and manuscript-preparation guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing a biomedical research manuscript (Summary, Introduction, Results, Discussion, STAR Methods) for submission to Cell, focusing on language, structure, argument strength, methodological transparency, and submission readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge editing support
rubrics_metrics.description: International publication guidelines such as ICMJE guidelines state that all non-author contributions, including editing, should be acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If satisfied with the quality of editing, add the following line in the acknowledgements section: 'We would like to thank Editage (www.editage.com) for English language editing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript structure and section ordering (Cell format)
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should be distinctly structured into the Summary, Introduction, Results, Discussion, and STAR Methods sections, as required by Cell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format, name, and order sections according to Cell requirements; prepare graphical abstract, author contributions, conflict of interest statements, and blurb for email alerts when applicable. Ensure layout and ordering conform to journal guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness in academic writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sufficient context but avoid excessive background information; streamline content so readers see only information directly relevant to the study objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce redundant or overly detailed background (e.g., avoid detailed stepwise developmental processes not central to the paper). Ensure word count adheres to Cell's specified limits. Eliminate unnecessary content to make space for essential items (e.g., ensure molecules studied are introduced in the Introduction if discussed later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate content allocation between Results and Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Results should state the results in a logical manner and should not contain background discussion or references to previous studies; Discussion should interpret results in the context of prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move background information from Results into Introduction or Discussion as suitable. Avoid discussing results within the Results section; reserve interpretation and comparison with literature for the Discussion. Cell discourages redundancy between Results and Discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary must state rationale, objective, and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summary should clearly state the rationale and objective before delving into methods and findings, and should highlight the significance of the findings and end with their implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rephrase/reorganize the Summary to present the research problem, what was done, main findings, and implications, concluding with the broader impact to pique editor and cross-disciplinary interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight multidisciplinary relevance and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: For journals with a broad readership (like Cell), the manuscript must discuss how findings are relevant across disciplines and possible clinical or translational significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state multidisciplinary relevance (e.g., potential implications for ectodermal dysplasia therapies) and include these implications in both the Summary and the cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure correspondence among title, rationale, objective, and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Title, Summary, Results, and Discussion should consistently reflect the central focus of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide on the paper's primary focus (e.g., general role of Sox21 in tooth development vs. ameloblast-to-hair transdifferentiation) and revise the title and text to maintain a consistent narrative. Example suggested titles: 'Sox21-mediated regulation of ectodermal organ determination' or 'Sox21-Anapc10 axis influences ameloblast identity.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal Discussion should begin with a short introductory paragraph stating the study aim and main findings, then discuss individual results in the context of previous studies, state limitations, and present the way forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an introductory orienting paragraph; for contradictions with prior work, offer possible explanations; list methodological/design-related limitations and connect them to future research directions. Ensure the discussion ends with a strong 'take-home message'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and coherence of the core argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas across manuscript sections must be connected so readers move seamlessly from one section to the next; avoid disconnected emphases (e.g., title highlighting a finding that Discussion downplays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reorder results to group related topics; highlight the main unexpected or important findings consistently across title, Summary, and Discussion; ensure Summary clearly states rationale and objective to orient readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological transparency and sufficient detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological details of study design, data collection, and analytical approaches must be reported transparently to enable replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include total number of animals used, sex, average age and weight, maintenance conditions (food/water, housing, light/dark, humidity, temperature), primers and qPCR cycling conditions, and other specific protocols. Ensure required ethics statements and major experimental methods are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical information must be clearly presented to support interpretation of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report statistical tests used, sample sizes, measures of variation, significance thresholds, and any software/packages used for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures, tables, and citation order
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables and figures must be relevant, correctly prepared, and cited in sequential order in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check figure/table formatting, ensure sequential citation in text, and fix minor issues flagged by the editor. Verify that figure legends contain the information required by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference accuracy and correspondence with in-text citations
rubrics_metrics.description: References must be accurate and correspond correctly with in-text citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check each reference for correctness and consistency with citation style; ensure no missing or mismatched citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter content
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter should highlight the significance of the study findings and include implications, declarations, and statements required by the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the cover letter to pique interest (emphasize conceptual advances and multidisciplinary relevance) and include required declarations (conflict of interest, ethics, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to journal word limits and formatting details
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript must comply with journal-specified word limits and formatting (naming/ordering of sections, layout).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim content where necessary to meet word limits; address formatting items the editor cannot change (e.g., graphical abstract preparation) and follow Cell's layout specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid redundancy and extraneous mentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate repetitive information and mentions of molecules or topics that are not referred to later in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a molecule (e.g., Shh, Anapc10) is studied, ensure it is introduced in the Introduction; remove mentions of molecules that are not discussed later to prevent distraction and maintain focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript organization: ordering of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Order the Results so related topics are grouped together and separate topics remain distinct, preserving logical flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rearrange result sections to keep themes together (e.g., group all results about Sox21’s role in teeth separately from those about Sox21-Anapc10 influence on ameloblast identity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate with editor and post-edit workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with the editor after editing: respond to editor comments, request revisions checks, provide feedback, and inform the editing service about acceptance or dissatisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to editor comments or send questions to the editor; ask for revisions to be checked before submission; give feedback on the job and report if not satisfied or if paper is accepted. Consider adding the editor to favorites for future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize the 'take-home message'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Discussion should end with a concise, strong take-home message highlighting the most important findings and their implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit final paragraph that crystallizes the study's main contribution, multidisciplinary relevance, potential clinical significance, and directions for future research.
